result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_matching()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of edges forms a valid matching. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22165-L22240){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_matching(edges) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A matching is a set of edges where no two edges share a common endpoint (node). This is useful for validating matchings or checking matching constraints. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs or edge labels to check. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the edges form a valid matching (no shared endpoints), `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two disjoint edges (`A-B` and `C-D`) share no endpoints, so together they form a valid matching: ::: {#3d582022 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("C", "D") ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() # Returns True (no shared endpoints) graph.is_matching(edge_ids) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: In a path `A-B-C`, the two edges share node `B`, so they don't form a valid matching: ::: {#1c3699f8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() # Returns False (B is shared) graph.is_matching(edge_ids) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: This makes it easy to sanity-check the output of matching algorithms like `maximal_matching()`: ::: {#0cdc7e32 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(6) matching = graph.maximal_matching() # Returns True: maximal_matching() always produces a valid matching graph.is_matching(matching) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
